q: Slepian-Wolf theorem for distributed source coding allows two correlated sources X,Y to be compressed separately (without seeing each other) and decoded jointly at rates:
opts: R_X ≥ H(X|Y), R_Y ≥ H(Y|X), and R_X+R_Y ≥ H(X,Y)
exp: Slepian-Wolf: the achievable rate region for separate encoding, joint decoding of (X,Y) is R_X ≥ H(X|Y), R_Y ≥ H(Y|X), R_X+R_Y ≥ H(X,Y). Remarkably, this matches the rate for joint encoding—correlation can be exploited even without communication between encoders.
